NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Election Commission to decide at the earliest which of the two rival factions of the All India Trinamool Congress will get the party's name and symbol.Hearing a plea filed by Mamata Banerjee , the top court asked the poll panel to inform it by Monday when it expected to take a final decision on the dispute.The Supreme Court also referred to the Shiv Sena factional dispute and said the row between the two AITC factions should be decided expeditiously.The development comes days after the Election Commission temporarily allotted Mamata Banerjee's faction the name "Mamata All India Trinamool Congress" and the "football player" symbol.The rival faction was allotted the name "Democratic Trinamool Congress" and the "envelope" symbol.Earlier, in an interim order, the poll panel froze the All India Trinamool Congress name and its "flowers and grass" symbol after recognising a factional dispute within the party. Neither faction can use the original name or symbol until the dispute is finally settled.The temporary arrangement will apply to the upcoming bypolls, with candidates of the two factions contesting under the separate names and symbols allotted by the Commission.The Election Commission has been hearing competing claims over control of the party, its name and election symbol. Both sides have submitted documents and appeared before the Commission during the proceedings.The dispute reached the poll panel after rival groups staked claims to control the TMC. The commission subsequently sought submissions on issues including organisational control, authorised office-bearers, party assets, the party name and its election symbol.
Article Summary: The supreme court asked the election commission to decide at the earliest which of the two rival factions of the all india trinamool congress will get the party's name and symbol. The top court asked the poll panel to inform it by monday when it expected to take a final decision on the dispute.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu Pocso case: Businessman Veeramani, aide arrested; what we know so far

NEW DELHI: The Central Crime Branch (CCB) has arrested Ganesan, a longtime aide of granite businessman and Gem Granites chief Veeramani, in connection with a POCSO case involving the alleged sexual abuse of minor girls.Ganesan is the fourth accused arrested in the case. Police said he had worked with Veeramani’s Gem Granites for 23 years and is currently employed with Balaji Global Enterprises.According to investigators, Ganesan had video clips on his mobile phone that purportedly showed Veeramani in an obscene act involving a minor girl. Police said he did not inform the authorities about the videos.The CCB is now investigating how Ganesan came to possess the clips and why he allegedly kept them without alerting police. Investigators are also examining his mobile phone to determine whether any data was deleted.Veeramani was arrested on August 29 along with two alleged accomplices after the Anti-Vice Squad (AVS) registered a case over the alleged rape of minor girls. The three accused were subsequently remanded in Puzhal Central Prison.Police said the case came to light after a USB drive containing a video clip purportedly showing Veeramani sexually assaulting a juvenile girl was recovered.Investigators identified the survivor and established that she was a minor when the alleged offence took place in 2019.The video was also examined as part of the investigation into the allegations against Veeramani.The investigation has also expanded to suspected financial transactions allegedly made to influence the earlier probe, police said.Investigators are examining bank transactions and the possible involvement of intermediaries in the movement of funds.The ruling TVK on Wednesday demanded that DMK president MK Stalin explain how the POCSO case involving Veeramani was handled when the DMK was in power, alleging that the investigation was allowed to weaken and questioning why a final report was filed.The TVK alleged that the case had been “buried”. The party also questioned former law minister S. Regupathy over his handling of video footage submitted in connection with the case.“Under whose pressure did the then Law Minister Regupathy allow the investigation to be weakened? What was the reason?” the TVK asked.The party also sought an explanation for the filing of the final report, alleging that it was submitted without a proper investigation.

NEW DELHI: An NIA court in Delhi Wednesday granted bail to six Ukrainian nationals arrested in March this year for allegedly running a training camp for ethnic armed rebels in India and Myanmar.The court, which ordered their release on a cash bond of Rs 1 lakh each, also discharged them from offences under the Immigration and Foreigners Act following after the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO), which deals with the immigration matters involving foreign nationals, settled the offences on payment of a penalty of Rs 5.5 lakh each.The offences, which pertained to illegal entry and visa violations, are compoundable at the level of the FRRO.Special judge Prashant Sharma granted them default bail on grounds of parity with their American co-accused Matthew Aaron Van Dyke.While granting bail to Dyke on Sept 18, the judge had dismissed the NIA’s opposition, observing that even if the probe was far from over, “at this stage it cannot be concluded that applicant/ accused Matthew Aaron Vandyke is not entitled for default bail”.Default bail is provisioned in the UAPA if the probe agency doesn’t file charge sheet containing offences under the anti-terror law with 180 days of arresting the accused. Following this, the court had directed that the other six accused could also seek default bail.Earlier this month, the agency filed a charge sheet which did not mention provisions of the UAPA, 1967, which was invoked in the initial FIR.

Article Title: Painkillers for every ache? CDSCO warns of kidney risks, antibiotic misuse
Article Text:
CDSCO warns against misuse of painkillers, antibiotics over kidney disease risk. (Photo: ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Taking painkillers repeatedly for everyday aches or antibiotics without proper medical advice could put people at risk of kidney complications and other adverse effects, prompting the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) to issue a fresh advisory on their rational use.The drug regulator has asked people not to take non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), commonly used as painkillers, repeatedly or for prolonged periods without medical advice. It has also cautioned against self-medication with antibiotics and advised people with existing kidney disease or other risk factors for renal impairment to inform their doctor before taking NSAIDs.Prof Sandeep Mahajan, nephrologist at AIIMS, said that unregulated and prolonged use of painkillers can accelerate the decline in kidney function, particularly in people with chronic kidney disease. “All prescription medicines should be taken under the supervision of a qualified physician, with the prescribed dose and duration strictly followed. Medicines from alternative systems should also be used with caution, as some may contain substances that can be toxic to the kidneys. ”“Misuse of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs can cause serious kidney injury, particularly in people with pre-existing kidney disease.Even short-term use can be risky in vulnerable individuals,” said Dr Dinesh Khullar, Group Chairman, Nephrology & Renal Transplant Medicine, Max Super Speciality Hospital, Saket. “People should therefore avoid unnecessary self-medication and take these medicines only on medical advice. ”The warning comes against the backdrop of a substantial chronic kidney disease burden in India. A 2025 systematic review of community-based studies estimated pooled chronic kidney disease prevalence at 13.24%, although estimates varied widely across regions and studies.The CDSCO circular, issued on Monday, says NSAIDs and antibiotics are prescription medicines under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules and should be used only when clinically indicated, at the appropriate dose and duration and under medical supervision.The regulator has advised doctors to use the lowest effective dose of NSAIDs for the shortest appropriate duration, with extra caution in patients at risk of kidney injury. It has also urged judicious antibiotic use, avoiding unnecessary combinations, incorrect dosing and prolonged treatment.The National Centre for Disease Control's 2024 surveillance across 66 tertiary-care institutions found excessive consumption of “Watch” antibiotics, which have a higher resistance potential, along with inadequate use of “Access” antibiotics recommended as first-line treatment. The report also flagged inconsistent implementation of antimicrobial stewardship programmes.Self-medication remains common in India, with analgesics, antipyretics and antibiotics among the frequently self-medicated drugs. Pharmacists and retailers have been asked to enforce prescription rules, while hospitals and state regulators have been told to strengthen oversight and awareness of the risks, including kidney complications and antimicrobial resistance.
Article Summary: Cdsco warns against misuse of painkillers, antibiotics over kidney disease risk. Self-medication remains common in india, with analgesics, antipyretics and antibiotics among the frequently self-medicated drugs. A 2025 systematic review of community-based studies estimated pooled chronic kidney disease prevalence at 13.24%.

Article Title: After split verdict, SC refers law on EC appointment to larger bench; decision comes amid row over EC functioning
Article Text:
SC: Constitution bench should deal with case to prevent delay

SC: Constitution bench should deal with case to prevent delay

NEW DELHI: On a day when Election Commission found itself under the scanner, a two-judge bench of Supreme Court gave a split verdict on whether the issue of validity of the law on appointment of CEC/ECs be referred to a constitution bench, but later agreed to refer the case to a larger bench for the sake of early adjudication of the contentious issue.Validity of several provisions of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 has been challenged on the ground that the law gives the executive "overwhelming" power to appoint its nominee as election commissioner, as the selection panel composed of the PM, a Cabinet minister and the leader of the opposition is designed to give govt a 2:1 majority. The petitioners contended that EC's independence would be compromised in this process.The 2023 law was framed to replace an SC verdict which had directed that selection be done by a committee of the PM, CJI and leader of the opposition until Parliament determined the composition by passing a law. "Speaking in one voice would have better served institutional cohesion. Unfortunately, the court is divided in its opinion," a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and S C Sharma said.The hearing in the case went on for five days and at the fag end of proceedings, the Centre had sought referral of the case to a constitution bench.Noting that appointment of CEC/ECs was being litigated for last 11 years in SC after a petition was filed in 2015, the bench decided that the case should not be referred to a three-judge bench, which is the normal procedure, but to a constitution bench to settle the issue once and for all. It reasoned that a decision by a three-judge bench would be of little worth and only delay adjudication of the significant issue(s) that these writ petitions raise."Thus, we direct that the papers be placed before the CJI for considering the desirability of constituting a constitution bench of such number of judges to decide the question of vires of Sec 7 and the other provisions of Act," the bench said.The bench expressed hope that the case would be given priority as the issues raised were of "foundational importance to the democratic fabric of the country and its citizenry"."Petitioners seem to be justified in expressing their anxiety that references to five-judge benches remain unresolved for years. If statistics are any guide, none can say with any reasonable degree of certainty when long-pending references will get resolved. Undisputedly, this is an area of grave concern and the inordinate delay in resolution of the references is itself a source of institutional embarrassment which all stakeholders ought to strive to avoid. Self-introspection, indeed, is required," it said."We, thus, take this opportunity of requesting the Chief Justice to also explore the necessity of constituting a permanent five-judge bench to decide pure constitutional issues. This is not something novel that we are saying. It has been opined time and again by responsible citizens and we simply endorse their opinion. Given that resolving constitutional issues is the primary task of judges of this court, that must remain its core priority.Pendency of references for far too long, any period between five and 20 years or more, does not reflect well on the institution. It is time that the institution addresses the issue with the urgency and promptitude it deserves," the bench said.
Article Summary: Sc: constitution bench should deal with case to prevent delay in adjudication. Election commission found itself under the scanner on a day when it was under scrutiny. Justices dipankar datta and s c sharma said the court is divided in its opinion.

Article Title: SIR queries raised, but pertained to draft stage; focusing on some notes while ignoring others gives only one part of picture: EC
Article Text:
Dr. Sukhbir Singh Sandhu, Gyanesh Kumar, Dr. Vivek Joshi

Focusing on some notes while ignoring others gives only one part of picture: EC

_

NEW DELHI: Faced with criticism for election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi being cut out of crucial decisions, the Election Commission on Wednesday said the “operational queries, inputs and suggestions” raised over the past 10 months by the two commissioners, including on the special intensive revision (SIR) process, remained limited to the draft stages and were part of the standard administrative practice and decision-making process at the Commission.All decisions taken by the commission in the past one year, including SIR, “are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full commission,” EC asserted in a statement rebutting the contention that the chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar was acting unilaterally.EC was reacting to a report in Indian Express claiming that the two election commissioners had objected to steps taken by the poll panel on 14 occasions over 10 months, including the changes made to Form 6 as part of SIR, restricting field officers’ access to electoral roll databases and even regarding postings and foreign tours involving EC personnel.Sandhu and Joshi even wrote to the Cabinet secretary separately on July 29, complaining about redistribution of work by the senior deputy election commissioner (DEC) in charge of administration EC and the resultant centralisation of decision -making , said the report.In its statement, EC said that differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberation in any institution before a final decision is taken.“Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks and balances are standard, ongoing practices to ensure transparency, legal compliance and operational rigour." EC said all its actions as well as official orders, decisions and administrative decisions have been in accordance with laws and commission's instructions and carry full legal sanction."Highlighting certain specific internal notes/observations spread over the period of 10 months while overlooking the much larger body of approvals, decisions, instructions and initiatives give only one part of the picture," EC said adding that its decisions, instructions, 40 new initiatives and conduct of polls in six states/UTs in the past one year were all based on unanimous decisions by the commission in the past one year.Sources in EC said the objections were largely raised in written notes sent by the election commissioners to the deputy election commissioners (DECs), in many cases after they had signed on the concerned file following a unanimous decision; including in the cases of changes made to Form 6. The two commissioners, Joshi in May and Sandhu in August, had argued that changes in Form 6 could be carried out only by the government. However, sources maintained, after they along with the CEC unanimously approved the file relating to SIR orders for Bihar (Phase 1) and then a dozen states (Phase 2), which listed the revised Form 6 and the accompanying declaration on citizenship. In fact, by the time Sandhu objected, the Supreme Court had already upheld the validity of SIR as well as the processes followed by EC, sources said.As part of his case against powers getting centralised and CEC not taking his two colleagues in confidence, Sandhu had raised the issue of who had authorised filing of appeals on EC's behalf before the SIR tribunals in West Bengal. Sources, however, told TOI that this was as per the Supreme Court order dated April 1, 2026, particularly para 9 that stated that appeals may be filed by "persons whose names have been excluded from the voters list" or "by the authorities of the ECI, who may be aggrieved by the inclusion of names by the adjudicatory authorities".On the commissioners’ alleged objection to centralisation of the electoral roll database or ERONet/ECINet, allegedly with restricted access to field officers like the electoral registration officers (EROs) to decide on addition of deletion of names, the Commission said digital platforms such as ECINet operate under strict data security protocols to prevent unauthorised tampering, manipulation, etc. "IT security checks and audit controls are standard cybersecurity measures implemented across national databases. Statutory authorities, including EROs and district election officers (DEOs), function as per statutory powers for registration and deletion under law,” said EC. Sources in EC told TOI that while EROs and DEOs may have faced access issues due to system errors on some occasions, they have full access to electors databases and have been deciding on roll updations during SIR.Sources in the Commission did not contest Joshi's claim that agenda and minutes of EC meetings were not being circulated, but said this has been the norm before the present commission assumed office.Responding to the objections to decision of the DEC (Administration) to change the officer in charge of IT division, sources said that powers to decide appointment, recruitment, transfers and postings of officers above the level of section officer and posting and transfer of personal staff of election commissioners and DECs were delegated to DEC (Administration) in 1997.Regarding Joshi's April 16 objection to EC officers being sent on foreign trips without the "commission's" approval, sources said the power in this regard has been with the CEC since long.Reacting to Sandhu's objection that he had learnt of EC's new IT modules, portals etc from the media, sources pointed that both Sandhu and Joshi were present at ECINet's launch on January 22.
Article Summary: Election commission responds to criticism of two election commissioners. S s sandhu and vivek joshi were accused of being cut out of crucial decisions. Ec says the objections were largely raised in written notes sent by the election commissioners to the deputy election commissioners (decs) sources in the commission did not contest joshi's claim that agenda and minutes of ec meetings were not being circulated.

He said SC has clearly ruled that all election commissioners, including the CEC, function on equal footing, and the revelations about the watchdog's functioning show that election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, who dissented against the CEC were in a majority.

Article Title: J&K elected govt has no say in book ban: Omar Abdullah
Article Text:
Omar Abdullah

SRINAGAR: J&K CM Omar Abdullah said Wednesday his elected govt had no role in deciding which books are banned or withdrawn from libraries, distancing his administration from the removal of 4,249 books after a screening of more than 21 lakh volumes across the Union territory over the past two months.“I have my own views on whether books should be banned or not. But unfortunately, in the current system we in the elected govt don’t get to decide these things,” Omar said. “Then we will take a fresh look at what’s happening,” he said, referring to a future change in the administrative set-up.Home department, which handles law and order and security in the Union territory, reports directly to lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha. Omar did not clarify whether the book-removal order came from home department or education department under elected govt.A year ago, home department banned 25 books on Kashmir for allegedly promoting “a false narrative”, “secessionism” and “anti-national” views. The total number of banned and withdrawn books swelled to 518 since then.Omar’s remarks came after Hurriyat Conference chairperson Mirwaiz Umar Farooq questioned who decided that thousands of books, including almost 4,000 from the Kashmir region, were objectionable and demanded that their titles and reasons for removal be made public. Writing on X, he asked: “By withdrawing these books whose agenda is the elected govt implementing, its own or someone else’s?”Farooq held Omar govt responsible because education department and universities separately ordered in July screening of all new and old books in offices, classrooms, staff rooms and libraries for “objectionable content” after home department withdrew two volumes it called “highly inappropriate”. More than 21 lakh books were screened and over 4,000 titles removed from libraries since the orders were issued, education minister Sakina Itoo told the assembly Tuesday.
Article Summary: Omar abdullah said elected govt had no role in deciding which books are banned or withdrawn from libraries. He distanced his administration from the removal of 4,249 books after a screening of more than 21 lakh volumes across the union territory. Omar did not clarify whether the book-removal order came from home department or education department.

Article Title: 'UP ke ladke' in for political 'brawl'? SP, Congress spar over who can beat BJP in 2027

NEW DELHI: The "UP ke ladke" bonhomie is beginning to look less like a united front and more like a contest for the upper hand, with Congress and Samajwadi Party leaders trading jabs over who can take on the BJP in Uttar Pradesh. With the 2027 assembly election approaching, are cracks emerging in the INDIA bloc's battle plan against Yogi Adityanath's BJP?SP MP Iqra Hasan set off the latest bout of sparring by saying Congress "can't achieve much on its own" and projecting party boss and former CM Akhilesh Yadav as the only leader capable of defeating the BJP in Uttar Pradesh.Her remarks drew a quick response from the Congress, with party leaders pushing back against the suggestion that the SP could take on the BJP by itself.Congress MP Imran Masood said, "She (Iqra Hasan) also cannot do it alone. What is the problem with that? Iqra is our child. She is like our niece.""People from the Trinamool Congress were also saying a lot. Look at what happened in Bengal. Let us move together, and we will remain in peace," he added with a reference to Mamata-led TMC's big defeat in Bengal after contesting solo.Congress leader Udit Raj pointed to the SP's performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha election while questioning Iqra's claim."That may be her (Iqra Hasan's) own statement, but we can understand this through an example: when the alliance was formed in 2024, the Samajwadi Party won 36 seats. What was its performance before that? The Samajwadi Party had only six MPs in 2019. So, in politics, one plus one does not always make two; one plus one can make eleven.Therefore, I think she should correct her understanding," Udit Raj told IANS.The saffron party, meanwhile, was quick to weigh in on the disagreement. Uttar Pradesh BJP vice-president Neeraj Singh said, "Congress will not be able to achieve anything on its own across the country. And even if it forms an alliance with the Samajwadi Party or any other party in Uttar Pradesh, the people of Uttar Pradesh have already formed an alliance in their hearts with the BJP government..."Iqra, who made the remarks on Monday, had said, "It is an absolutely foolish statement. I think that if there is anyone in Uttar Pradesh who can defeat the BJP, it is only Akhilesh Yadav. Congress will not be able to do anything on its own. If the alliance remains, it will be very good; if it does not, it is a loss for them (Congress), not for us."The "UP ke ladke" chemistry that helped Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav pull off a striking upset in the 2024 Lok Sabha election has yet to turn into a clear seat-sharing formula for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly polls.The two leaders have continued to share the stage on occasions, including protest for students, maintaining a public show of camaraderie. But behind that familiar chemistry, the alliance arithmetic is still taking shape.There has been no concrete discussion on how the 403 assembly seats could be divided between Congress and the Samajwadi Party.Their partnership took shape months before the 2024 Lok Sabha election, and the results that followed gave the alliance a strong political imprint.The SP contested 62 of the state's 80 Lok Sabha seats and won 37, including Faizabad, the constituency covering Ayodhya. Congress fought 17 seats and won six. Together, the two parties crossed the halfway mark of UP's Lok Sabha tally, handing the BJP a major setback in a state that sends the most MPs to Parliament.For the SP, it was very much the bigger share of the alliance pie. Akhilesh's party emerged as the largest opposition force in the state, and second largest in country, while Congress revived its presence with six seats.The result also had a powerful political backdrop. Uttar Pradesh is the home turf of chief minister Yogi Adityanath and the parliamentary constituency of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The BJP had also invested enormous political capital in Ayodhya, where the Ram temple consecration took place in January 2024 in the presence of PM Modi and RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat.Yet, months later, the BJP lost the Faizabad seat to the SP.The result turned Rahul and Akhilesh into the "UP ke ladke" of the 2024 campaign, a political pairing that seemed to have found the right formula for the state's electorate. But as the next election approaches, the partnership is facing a different kind of test: Seat-sharing.Akhilesh has repeatedly said that the SP will contest the 2027 election with the INDIA bloc partners with whom it fought the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, effectively keeping the door open for Congress. But Congress has not made a similar formal commitment. Neither Rahul Gandhi nor party president Mallikarjun Kharge has publicly announced a seat-sharing arrangement with the SP.Meanwhile, the SP is already getting its electoral machinery moving.Sources told TOI that the party's top leadership has finalised candidates for more than 100 of the 403 assembly seats, while the process is under way for the remaining constituencies. The party has not yet released a formal candidate list.SP strategists say the early exercise is deliberate, giving prospective candidates time to prepare their constituencies, build networks and hit the ground running once the campaign begins.The strategy is not entirely new. Political observers point out that the SP followed a similar approach before the 2022 assembly and 2024 Lok Sabha elections, beginning the candidate-selection process well ahead of polling but releasing the actual lists only a few months before the election.Congress, meanwhile, has indicated that it is preparing to contest all 403 seats. That ambition could make the eventual negotiatins with the SP considerably more interesting.And there is another piece on the chessboard. AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi has made an open offer to Akhilesh, potentially bringing another party into the opposition's seat-sharing calculations.If the SP chooses to engage with Owaisi, the equation could become even more complicated for an alliance that has so far largely revolved around SP and Congress.The Lok Sabha 2024 friendship was a renewed one. Just two years earlier, the grand old party and Akhilesh Yadav’s Samajwadi Party had contested the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections separately, as they sought to take on Yogi Adityanath, who was then seeking a second term as chief minister.Yogi comfortably retained his Lucknow throne, while the Samajwadi Party increased its numbers. The Congress, however, suffered a major setback, winning just 2 of the 403 assembly seats.Rahul, personally, also appeared hesitant when it came to announcing the Mahagathbandhan’s chief ministerial face in Bihar last year.He also appeared to have reservations about Tejashwi Yadav’s eagerness to project himself as the alliance’s face, as well as over seat-sharing, with a large chunk of seats going to Lalu Yadav’s Rashtriya Janata Dal.A similar story could now unfold in Uttar Pradesh, where the Congress may look to expand its footprint with an eye on the next Lok Sabha elections. Uttar Pradesh remains at the heart of national politics, making a strong presence in the state crucial for any party with larger ambitions.Akhilesh Yadav, meanwhile, would be looking to return to power in Lucknow and reclaim the chief minister’s chair.Congress’ delayed decisions and its cautious approach towards trusting allies have also been visible more recently in Tamil Nadu. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh and RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav have previously urged the Congress to show a “big heart” and back “regional players” in their home turfs.So, while the Rahul-Akhilesh bond now may still look intact in public, the real test could come away from the cameras: How many seats each party wants, how many it is willing to give up, and whether the "UP ke ladke" formula can survive the hard arithmetic of 2027.The BJP under Yogi Adityanath, meanwhile, is preparing to defend its position in Uttar Pradesh and seek another term in the state's 403-member assembly, ensuring that the opposition's alliance arithmetic will remain under close watch.With a third consecutive term in Uttar Pradesh, Yogi would match former CM Mulayam Singh Yadav's record of three consecutive terms in the state, while he already holds the record for the longest uninterrupted tenure as UP chief minister, having been in office for nearly a decade.
Article Summary: 'up ke ladke' vs each other? Sp-congress spar over who can beat bjp in 2027. Iqra hasan ’s remarks trigger congress pushback.bjp joins sp-cong war of words. There has been no concrete discussion on how the 403 assembly seats could be divided between congress and the samajwadi party.

Article Title: 'Bihar, Maharashtra, Delhi, Haryana & West Bengal': Oppn seeks fresh polls after EC 'dissent' report

NEW DELHI: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav on Wednesday accused the Election Commission of being misused to benefit the BJP and alleged that election rules had been changed to weaken the Opposition’s ability to challenge poll results.At a press conference, Tejashwi questioned the functioning of the poll panel, raised concerns over changes to the retention period for voting and counting records, and demanded fresh elections in Bihar and Bengal. He also called for the removal of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“Whether it is the results in Bihar or Maharashtra, Delhi, Haryana, or Bengal—the opposition has not lost. Rather, in these states, the EC has been misused to ensure that the BJP wins,” he said.He alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah had “flouted all the rules” and claimed the CEC had acted according to their wishes.“And this process is still continuing. It is going on in several states, and it is being carried out arbitrarily. There are objections from two Election Commissioners as well. Even then, neither Modi ji nor Amit Shah ji is coming forward and saying anything about it,” he said.He also questioned the change in the period for retaining voting and counting records. He said the earlier period of up to one year had been reduced to 45 days.“That means, when there is no evidence left, what can the opposition do? When they go to court, there will be no evidence, so there will be no benefit,” he said.On the appointment of the CEC, Tejashwi said the earlier selection panel included the Chief Justice of India, while a Union minister is now part of the panel.“This means that, as Modi ji wishes, one Gyanesh ji may be removed, but the BJP can bring in another Gyanesh Kumar,” he said.He also alleged that elections in Bihar and Bengal had been illegal and demanded fresh polls in both states.Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi also hit out at the Election Commission over the alleged irregularities, calling “vote chori” a crime against Indian voters and an attack on the Constitution.“Vote chori is a crime against the Indian people and a direct attack on our constitution. The BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason. Justice will be served,” he said.DMK supremo and former Tamil Nadu chief minister MK Stalin also demanded the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. He cited allegations over the functioning of the EC during the special intensive revision of electoral rolls.Stalin said the DMK and other opposition parties had opposed the deletion of voters from electoral rolls under the SIR exercise. He said the process, carried out months before elections in different states, had faced allegations of irregularities, particularly in West Bengal.He said, "The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, along with other Opposition parties, has consistently opposed the move to delete crores of voters from the electoral rolls in the name of the Special Intensive Revision (#SIR). Rushed through just months ahead of elections in State after State, the exercise was riddled with irregularities and sparked widespread unrest, particularly in West Bengal."Stalin said the reported objections by election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi over decisions related to SIR raised questions about the functioning of the three-member poll panel. Responding to a report by the Indian Express, he claimed the two commissioners had been kept unaware of key decisions and that their objections had been brushed aside on 14 occasions in 10 months."Gyanesh Kumar had been acting unilaterally and in secrecy, without the concurrence of the other two election commissioners. Even more alarming is the revelation that Thiru. Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Thiru."Stalin said the EC's decisions should follow the majority view when its members disagree. He argued that concerns raised by two serving commissioners could not be treated merely as an internal or procedural issue."Where the commissioners differ in opinion on any matter, the decision must be based on the majority view. If two of its three members were themselves kept unaware of what was being done in the commission’s name, this cannot be dismissed as a mere internal or procedural matter. It constitutes a grave assault on Indian democracy," he said.The DMK chief also raised questions over electoral-roll appeals filed even after courts had directed that certain voters be added to the rolls. He questioned who authorised and filed such appeals.Stalin said the party had earlier moved an impeachment motion against Gyanesh Kumar and demanded that he step down.“Gyanesh Kumar must go immediately. The SIR exercise must be halted,” Stalin said, while calling for a “fair and thorough investigation” into the functioning of the Election Commission.Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee also attacked the Election Commission over the reported objections by the two commissioners to decisions linked to the SIR process.Reacting to the Indian Express report, Mamata alleged that the poll panel had been misused and demanded action against Gyanesh Kumar.“This is such a scandalous story. We had never seen this in our lives. This election commissioner must be arrested. He has no moral authority to continue, and BJP must see that they cannot destroy our Constitution. They cannot demolish democracy,” she said.Mamata also alleged that people linked to the BJP had been deployed in the electoral-roll process and accused the CEC of misusing the police.“They cannot depute their own EROs in the name of BJP IT Team. What we said earlier has now been exposed,” she said.She further said, “Gyanesh Kumar has misused Police and with BJP they have deputed their own BJP-minded people. Such a scandal has never happened. If you have any honour, you yourself would ask to be arrested. You should be arrested.”Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also questioned the functioning of the Election Commission, saying the reported objections by two election commissioners had raised serious concerns over the poll panel's impartiality.Addressing a press conference in Lucknow, Akhilesh referred to reports that Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders concerning SIR and electoral-roll procedures.“This is dangerous for our democracy. This is an attempt to weaken our democracy,” he said.Akhilesh questioned whether elections held during a period when the Election Commission was allegedly not acting impartially could be considered fair.“This means that the governments which have been formed during this period are unconstitutional governments,” he said.In an earlier post on X, he described the reported objections by the two commissioners as “extremely serious news” and urged the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance of the matter.He also alleged that voters supporting the Samajwadi Party had been systematically removed from electoral rolls and claimed that no action was taken despite the party bringing the matter to the Election Commission's notice.“Samajwadi Party voters were systematically deleted from the Election Commission's voters list. We brought this to the notice of the Election Commission, but no action was taken against anyone.Rampant malpractice was committed on a massive scale in the by-elections,” he said.The EC has rejected the suggestion that its decisions were taken without the participation of all three commissioners. It said decisions, including those related to SIR, were taken unanimously with the approval of the CEC and the two other election commissioners.The poll panel said written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks were standard practices within a multi-member constitutional body. It said differing views were part of institutional deliberations before final decisions were taken and that all official orders had legal sanction and followed established procedures.
Article Summary: Opposition leaders have stepped up demands for action against the election commission. Calls for cec gyanesh kumar’s removal, an investigation into the poll panel's functioning and, in some states, fresh elections. Leaders have also questioned the sir exercise and alleged irregularities in electoral-roll revisions.

Article Title: EC 'dissent' row: Opposition seeks CEC's arrest, fresh polls in states; BJP lauds 'pure democracy' - top developments
Article Text:
SIR row explodes into political confrontation as Opposition demands action against CEC

Opposition demands CEC's removal, arrest

Fresh polls demanded in Bihar, West Bengal

Akhilesh, Omar question EC functioning

BJP says EC differences show ‘pure democracy’

EC says all decisions were unanimous

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The reported objections raised by two Election Commissioners to decisions linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls triggered a major political confrontation on Wednesday, with opposition parties demanding action against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, an immediate halt to the SIR exercise and fresh elections in states where polls have already been held.The ruling BJP, however, defended the Election Commission, saying differences expressed by Election Commissioners during internal deliberations showed that the poll panel was functioning democratically rather than under a “dictatorial” system.The political row followed a media report which said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR process and electoral rolls.The Election Commission has rejected the suggestion that the reported objections indicated a breakdown in its functioning.It said differing views and observations were a normal part of institutional deliberations and maintained that its decisions, including those concerning SIR, had been taken unanimously.Opposition parties, which have been criticising the EC over the SIR exercise, seized on the report to renew their demands for action against Gyanesh Kumar.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi reiterated his “vote chori” allegation against the Election Commission, describing it as “a crime against the people of India” and an attack on the Constitution.“The BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason. Justice will be served,” Rae Bareli MP said.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said 73 Opposition Rajya Sabha MPs had submitted a fresh notice on April 24, seeking Kumar's removal.He questioned whether the Rajya Sabha chairman would decide on the pending notice since the Monsoon Session of Parliament had not yet been prorogued.Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal went further, demanding that Kumar be removed and arrested.“Gyanesh Kumar should be immediately sacked and jailed,” Thackeray said.He also demanded that the last elections in Maharashtra, West Bengal and Tamil Nadu be nullified and fresh polls held in the three states using ballot papers.Kejriwal demanded that the entire SIR exercise be cancelled, all changes made under it be reversed and the voter list from three years ago be restored. He also called for Kumar's arrest and registration of a sedition case against him.TMC MP Derek O'Brien said, “Impeach CEC to save democracy.”Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee also demanded Kumar's arrest and said he had “no moral authority to continue”.“This is such a scandalous story. We had never seen this in our lives. This Election Commissioner must be arrested. He has no moral authority to continue, and the BJP must see that they cannot destroy our Constitution. They cannot demolish democracy,” Banerjee said.The Opposition's demands also extended to fresh elections in states where polls have already taken place.RJD leader and Bihar leader of opposition Tejashwi Yadav demanded fresh elections in Bihar and West Bengal, alleging that the electoral mandates in the two states had been compromised through electoral fraud and institutional manipulation.“The opposition did not lose elections on the ground; the results were orchestrated by PM Modi and Amit Shah. In 2020, we were defeated through manipulation, and the same script was executed in 2025. Voter lists were purged, money was distributed, and counting was manipulated. The electoral outcomes in Bihar and Bengal are fraudulent, and we demand that fresh, transparent elections be held,” he said.Yadav also questioned changes to the rules governing the preservation of voting and counting records, alleging that the period had been reduced from one year to 45 days.He said this could make it difficult for parties to approach courts without access to election-related evidence.DMK president M K Stalin demanded Kumar's resignation and an immediate halt to the SIR exercise. He also sought a fair probe “into everything that transpired within the EC and those responsible should be held accountable”, according to news agency PTI.Stalin alleged that the report had raised doubts about the results of Assembly elections held after the SIR exercise and said his party had consistently opposed the deletion of voters from electoral rolls in the name of SIR.Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said governments formed during a period when the Election Commission was not functioning impartially were “unconstitutional”.“This means that the governments which have been formed during this period are unconstitutional governments,” Yadav said.He alleged that interference in the poll panel amounted to “trampling” democracy and urged the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance of the matter.Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah said the Centre and the Election Commission needed to take corrective steps to prevent people from losing faith in elections.“Corrective action needs to be taken somewhere. Otherwise, if people lose faith in elections, what remains of a democracy? Elections are the very foundations of a democracy. If people lose faith in elections, why would they even participate in them? I feel the Election Commission and the government of India need to reflect on this,” Abdullah said.He also said the report raised questions about the functioning of the poll panel and referred to his earlier concerns over the electoral process.The BJP rejected the Opposition's allegations and defended the reported differences between the Election Commissioners.Addressing a press conference at the BJP headquarters, party spokesperson Sambit Patra said differing views during official deliberations showed that the poll panel was functioning democratically.“The media reports saying that the election commissioners shared differing views in official deliberations is a reflection of pure democracy,” Patra said.“If there is no communication and exchange of views among the election commissioners who conduct polls, the opposition parties would allege 'dictatorship' and call them 'yes men' of the government,” he said.Patra said the Election Commission's response showed that neither the poll panel nor other constitutional bodies were functioning under a “dictatorial rule”.“This shows that the Election Commission (EC) and all other constitutional bodies are functioning in a democratic manner and upholding the democracy of the country,” he said.Responding to the media report, the Election Commission said written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks and balances were standard practices within a multi-member constitutional body.“The ECI is a constitutional body that functions under the strict mandate of Article 324 of the Constitution, statutory rules and established institutional conventions. The Commission operates as a multi-member constitutional body. Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks-and-balances are standard, ongoing practices designed to ensure complete transparency, legal compliance and operational rigour,” it said.The commission said all official orders, decisions and administrative directions carried full legal sanction and followed established statutory procedures. It added that operational queries or inputs raised by members during the drafting stage were part of standard administrative practice aimed at safeguarding voter rights and improving electoral processes.The EC further said differing views and observations were a normal part of deliberation before a final decision was taken.“Not only the three Commissioners, but every officer of the Commission is fully authorised to give his suggestions to the Commission for improving the electoral system,” it said.The commission said focusing on specific internal notes and observations over 10 months while overlooking its wider body of approvals, decisions, instructions and initiatives presented only one part of the picture.It said it had taken numerous decisions, issued instructions and introduced around 40 new initiatives and electoral reforms, including electoral-roll revision and SIR across the country.“All these decisions are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full Commission in the past one year,” the EC said.The commission also pointed to the conduct of elections in Bihar, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam and West Bengal during the period and said it remained committed to carrying out its constitutional duties.
Article Summary: Sir row explodes into political confrontation as opposition demands action against cec.opposition demands cec's removal, arrest and fresh polls demanded in bihar, west bengal.bjp says ec differences show ‘pure democracy’ dmk president m k stalin demanded kumar's resignation and an immediate halt to the sir exercise.

Article Title: Allegations of transfer of BCI assets to trust matter of concern: Supreme Court
Article Text:
Bar Council of India chairman Manan Kumar Mishra.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court said Wednesday allegations of Bar Council of India's assets being transferred to a trust created by the BCI chairperson are a matter of concern and it has to be examined. SC also agreed to examine whether it has the power to establish and regulate law colleges and universities.The court was hearing petitions questioning the functioning of BCI-Pearl First Trust and the establishment of law colleges by the trust. It sought BCI's response on the issues within two weeks. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked how BCI can be considered an expert body to regulate legal education when law scholars and academics are better suited to deal with academic matters. "How can BCI regulate law colleges? That's the real question. Their statutory role comes into existence only after one gets a licence. So the issue is whether law schools can be regulated. We'd like to examine whether BCI has the power to control and regulate universities/law colleges," the bench said.Advocates Prashant Bhushan and Pranav Sachdeva, appearing for petitioner Girish Mittal, said BCI passed a resolution in 2016 and abolished an earlier trust and transferred the funds to a new trust 'Bar Council of India Trust for Promotion of Education, Legal and Professional Reforms and Improvement in Research'.They said the trust established one law college each in Goa and Andhra Pradesh. BCI, however, said the Bar body has passed a resolution providing that there would be no lifetime trustees and that the tenure of trustees would be coterminous with their membership of BCI.SC had earlier said BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra's position was only "pro tem" until a freshly constituted lawyers' body elects its office bearers. Mishra was first elected as BCI chairperson till 2012. Though he briefly demitted office in 2014, he returned as chairperson in Nov that year and has remained in the post since then.
Article Summary: Supreme court says allegations of bar council of india's assets being transferred to a trust created by the bci chairperson are a matter of concern. Sc also agreed to examine whether it has the power to establish and regulate law colleges and universities. It sought bci's response on the issues within two weeks.

Article Title: Cannot direct Speaker but expect early ruling on TMC rebels: Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Wednesday remarked that it expected Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla to take an "expeditious" decision on a plea seeking the disqualification of 20 rebel TMC MPs who have joined Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI).A bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said it was aware that it could not issue a direction to the Lok Sabha Speaker, "but we just want to remind him about an expeditious resolution".Senior advocate Kalyan Banerjee, representing TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee, submitted that the rebel parliamentarians had not filed a response despite notices being issued and had sought further extension.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Speaker, told SC that Birla had issued notices on the disqualification petitions. "He knows the seriousness of the matter," Mehta said.The CJI remarked, "We will expect anything which is required to be decided expeditiously, the very nature... demands early adjudication."Mehta responded, "Can a constitutional functionary remind another constitutional functionary of his constitutional duty?" He said the court should not prescribe a time limit for the Speaker.Justice Bagchi said, "...We may not give imperative directions, but keeping in mind the decision in the Keisham Meghachandra Singh case... have resolution of this issue expeditiously."In the 2020 case, SC had ruled that the speaker must decide defection cases within a reasonable time, preferably three months.Justice Bagchi asked Mehta to submit a timeline for the Speaker's decision. Mehta, however, said he could not give SC a commitment. "This court's monitoring may not be justified. I would urge not to fix the Speaker's schedule," he said.The top court recorded the submission of the rebel MPs that they would file a reply within four weeks and adjourned the matter.
Article Summary: Supreme court asks lok sabha speaker om birla to take an "expeditious" decision on a plea seeking the disqualification of 20 rebel tmc mps. Solicitor general tushar mehta, appearing for the speaker, told sc that birla had issued notices on the disqualifying petitions.

Article Title: Ensure govt benefits reach all eligible, PM Modi tells mantris
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi Wednesday asked all ministers to ensure the benefits of all govt schemes and programmes reach every eligible person and to work for society's overall development. At the Chintan Shivir meeting, Modi interacted with eight groups of eight ministers each, which deliberated on improving self-efficiency, delivery, effective communication and trust-based governance. TOI has learnt that the PM interacted with each group separately and the brainstorming session went on for nearly five hours at Seva Teerth.Ministers will resume the exercise Thursday. "PM went to each table to take part in the discussion and made suggestions as well. It was an altogether different experience," said a source.The two-day brainstorming session is aimed at stocktaking, improving coordination, preparing govt's future agenda and reviewing work underway on welfare schemes.
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi wednesday asked all ministers to ensure the benefits of all govt schemes and programmes reach every eligible person. The two-day brainstorming session is aimed at stocktaking, improving coordination, preparing govt's future agenda and reviewing work underway on welfare schemes.

Article Title: Judges appointing judges is a myth, says Justice Datta, points to way in which govt clears collegium picks
Article Text:
Judges appointing judges is a myth, says Justice Datta

NEW DELHI: Holding that the collegium system remains the most viable option for safeguarding judicial independence despite its "opacity and imperfections", Justice Dipankar Datta Wednesday said its deficiencies could not justify ushering in executive participation in collegium deliberations. He said judiciary had been relegated to playing second fiddle to the executive in appointments because of the way collegium recommendations were cleared by govt.Referring to govt's argument that the judiciary had an exclusive say in judges' appointments, Datta said "judiciary cannot always be at the receiving end" and devoted six pages to the issue, saying "relevant observations in response need to be made, lest the silence be misunderstood as a tacit acceptance by the court of such unworthy criticism in circulation".Datta said the executive wielded decisive control and held the reins over appointments at every level. He said it had become fashionable to blame the collegium for every infelicitous choice, conveniently forgetting that aberrations were exceptions and not the norm, and that no system could guarantee infallibility of human choice.The other judge on the bench, Justice S C Sharma said SG Tushar Mehta's submission was "not a criticism of the collegium system or regarding the role of executive in the appointment of judges"."It was a submission to the effect that if the constitution bench has held the presence of outsiders in collegium as violative of doctrine of separation of powers, a similar independence should be read in executive and rules framed under Art 324 be not declared void on the ground that it does not have an outsider in the selection committee or the executive predominates in it," he said.Sharma said the SG had based his argument on the judgment in the National Judicial Appointments Commission case, where a constitution bench held that the presence of even the law minister in the collegium for appointment of SC and HC judges would violate separation of powers. "Building upon the constitutional principle, the submission of the SG was that a corresponding degree of constitutional independence must be recognised for the executive as well as legislature. He submitted that the committee constituted under rules framed under Art 324 deserves to be declared legal though dominated by members of executive," Sharma said.Datta said, "The oft-repeated phrase that 'judges appoint judges' is a myth, which people have been fed by vested interests through motivated narratives. A sweeping generalisation that collegium acts as a law unto itself overlooks the consultative process envisaged under the Constitution, and the intrinsic role of executive - both at Centre and in the states."He added, "It is undeniable that collegium system has occasionally faltered and its functioning has not been free from aberrations. However, vociferous criticism, by itself, does not offer an alternative.While absence of an outsider may invite scrutiny, executive supremacy cannot be the cure. The constitutional quest is not to transfer primacy from one organ to another, but to preserve independence through checks and balances."What is worrying is that the sanctity of a collegium resolution is lost each time the executive implements it selectively, approving majority of those recommended while withholding one. Undeterred by piecemeal approvals and fate of those not cleared by the executive, collegium chooses to proceed, to avoid a head-on conflict with the executive, left with a Hobson's choice to keep the institution running. What it averts is a constitutional crisis; but the larger question is: how long can this state of affairs continue, if selective implementation is allowed to acquire the character of an accepted practice?"
Article Summary: Judges appointing judges is a myth, says justice datta. Datta: it had become fashionable to blame the collegium for every infelicitous choice. The other judge on the bench, justice s c sharma said sg tushar mehta's submission was "not a criticism of the collegium system"
